Title: Local pattern aware 3D video swin transformer with masked autoencoding for realtime augmented reality gesture interaction

swin transformer with masked 
autoencoding for realtime 
augmented reality gesture 
interaction
Suli Wang1,2
This study proposes a real-time augmented reality gesture interaction algorithm based on the Swin 
Transformer and a masked self-encoder. This algorithm solves the challenges of the traditional 
Transformer model regarding spatio-temporal feature extraction and real-time performance. During 
data preprocessing, the study uses a synthetic data annotation method to automatically generate 3D 
gesture images and annotate joint information, significantly improving data annotation efficiency. 
Using weighted Euclidean distance and structural similarity optimization, the paper proposes an image 
denoising model based on maximum a posteriori probability that effectively reduces noise interference 
in gesture image analysis. The gesture detection and segmentation module combines EfficientNet and 
Transformer models. It fuses shallow and deep features through skip connections, realizes multi-scale 
feature extraction, and enhances attention to the target area through the triplet attention module. 
Additionally, the paper introduces the local texture feature prior (RTHLBP) to optimize gesture 
recognition and segmentation accuracy. In the gesture classification module, the paper proposes a ViT 
architecture based on a masked autoencoder. It aligns features at different levels through a dynamic 
weight fusion strategy and combines the relative total variation map as a self-monitoring element. 
This significantly improves classification performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the 
proposed model’s accuracy, F1 score, and MIoU on the 4 GTEA sub-dataset surpass those of traditional 
CNN, Transformer, MobileNet, and DenseNet models, particularly on small datasets. The paper also 
optimizes the model’s real-time performance through a multi-core parallel computing strategy. 
Experiments show that as the number of DSP cores increases, the computation time is significantly 
reduced and the computational efficiency remains at a high level.
Keywords  Local pattern awareness, 3D video Swin transformer, Masked autoencoding, Real-Time 
augmented reality, Gesture recognition
Hands are one of the most effective and common ways of communication in human natural activities. People 
usually use their hands as the main means of perceiving and interacting with the world. Therefore, in order for 
machines to understand human hand activities, the human-computer interaction systems1–6 need to be able to 
detect hand gestures in real time and quickly, and need to be able to understand the way hands interact with the 
world, which is also crucial for semantically meaningful interpretation of human actions and behaviors. Modern 
industrial interaction systems have been developed towards virtual environments, such as the increasingly 
powerful virtual reality and augmented reality technologies. In this environment, natural interaction with virtual 
environments is particularly important. However, the technology for interacting with virtual environments still 
has some shortcomings. For example, gesture interaction in virtual environments requires the use of external 
objects such as the gloves, and hardware devices have problems such as occlusion and unclear recognition when 
recognizing gestures. According to the different ways of obtaining the gesture information, gesture interaction 
research can be divided into two categories:

Category 1: The contact-based gesture interaction framework, mainly including hardware configurations 
such as wearable devices.
Category 2: The non-contact gesture interaction framework mainly refers to the visual gesture interaction 
technology based on depth images or color images.
Since contact gesture interaction requires hardware devices as an aid, it limits the application scenarios. 
The framework based on non-contact is the mainstream of current research. Among them, vision-based 
gesture interaction technology is the main implementation method. Vision-based gesture interaction 
technology is to perform algorithmic analysis on hand images collected by depth cameras or color cameras to 
obtain corresponding algorithm results such as hand detection, gesture posture estimation, and hand action 
classification. The advantage of this technology is that it can effectively track and recognize gestures without 
restricting the user’s natural interaction. It is low-cost and suitable for large-scale popular applications. However, 
this technology is sensitive to usage environment, such as lighting conditions, hand occlusion, etc. To solve the 
above problems, this study proposes a new local pattern-aware 3D video Swin Transformer with masked auto-
encoding for real-time augmented reality gesture interaction.
The primary contribution of this study is:
	1.	 A gesture recognition algorithm based on Swin Transformer and masked self-encoding is proposed. This 
study innovatively combines the local attention mechanism of Swin Transformer to optimize the traditional 
Transformer model. At the same time, the fusion of masked self-encoding technology enables the model to 
learn spatial and temporal features more effectively. This operation can improve the accuracy and generali­
zation ability of gesture recognition.
	2.	 Optimized multi-core parallel computing strategy is studied. Aiming at the real-time requirements of 
augmented reality applications, this paper analyzes the changes in computing time and computing efficiency 
under different degrees of parallelism. At the same time, this paper proposes an optimization solution suita­
ble for multi-core architecture. This solution can reduce computing time while maintaining high computing 
efficiency as much as possible.
	3.	 Improved real-time performance and global stability of the gesture interaction is designed. The com­
parative experimental results show that this method can maintain high recognition accuracy under different 
data sets. At the same time, the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce latency and provide reliable tech­
nical support for augmented reality gesture interaction applications.
The novelty of the proposed method against existing Swin Transformer applications in gesture recognition are: 
(1) The traditional Swin Transformer focuses more on extracting global features when processing video gestures. 
This paper innovatively introduces a local pattern perception mechanism. This innovation enables the model 
to capture the local texture in gestures in a more fine-grained manner. (2) This paper combines the masked 
autoencoder technology to enhance the model’s self-supervised learning ability for the spatiotemporal sequence 
data.

Literature review
Review of augmented reality systems
Augmented reality technology has been widely used in many fields along with the development of immersive 
computer technology. Hidayat et al.7 studied the application of augmented reality technology in basic education. 
The study was based on a qualitative content analysis of ten articles from 2010 to 2020. The impact of augmented 
reality technology on primary school students’ learning outcomes was explored from a system level. Azimova 
and Solidjonov8 explored the role of augmented reality in English as a second language (ESL) teaching. As 
a typical example of the integration of AR and education, the study pointed out that traditional language 
teaching methods often lack interactivity and real-world application background. Augmented reality technology 
enables students to practice language in simulated real-world scenarios by superimposing digital content on 
the real world. Oyman et al.9 studied the integration of augmented reality and consumer behavior based on 
the technology acceptance model (TAM). This study used the structural equation model (SEM) to analyze 
consumers’ perception of augmented reality. The results showed that the perception of the augmented reality 
affected consumers’ pleasure and practicality.
Xu et al.10 studied the role of augmented reality in e-commerce. The study used a mixed methodology and 
analyzed the impact of augmented reality features on consumer behavior based on the stimulus-organism-
response (S-O-R) framework. The study revealed how augmented reality features enhance consumers’ shopping 
experience through a three-stage research design. Manurung et al.11 studied the application of augmented reality 
in primary school spatial modeling learning scheme. The study pointed out that geometric spatial modeling is 
essential for understanding the three-dimensional space. Augmented reality tools can combine virtual models 
with the real environments. This organic combination enables students to observe and manipulate geometric 
shapes intuitively. Marini et al.12 studied the impact of the combination of mobile augmented reality and 
metaverse on science classroom learning. Faqih and Jaradat13 conducted a comprehensive model based on task-
technology fit (TTF) theory and unified theory of fit (UTAUT2). The model studied the adoption behavior 
of augmented reality technology in education. Sarlin et al.14 studied positioning and mapping technology in 
augmented reality. The study pointed out that existing augmented reality benchmarks are often not realistic 
enough. This study proposed the LAMAR benchmark, which can better evaluate the localization and mapping 
capabilities of augmented reality.
Raja and Lakshmi Priya explored the role of comprehensive integration of information and communication 
technology, virtual reality and augmented reality in improving the quality of education. The study found that 
teachers generally recognized the potential of ICT, VR and AR in improving the educational environment, 
especially in distance education and online examinations, which can greatly improve efficiency. Voinea et al.15 
sorted out the research trends of industrial augmented reality from 2018 to 2022. These trends show that AR 
technology is increasingly used in the industrial field and is deeply integrated with smart manufacturing and 
artificial intelligence technologies. Marques et al.16 proposed a conceptual model and for analyzing and classifying 
collaborative augmented reality. The authors believe that AR technology can achieve seamless integration of 
virtual and reality. This advantage can promote the face-to-face or remote collaboration, and thereby enhancing 
team communication.
Review of gesture recognition algorithms
The advancement of gesture recognition technology has not only improved the way people interact with 
computers, but also greatly affected the process of computer-assisted analysis. Guo et al.17 outlined the 
application of gesture recognition in HMI. The study emphasized the limitations of traditional HMI methods, 
such as the need for a fixed operating space for mouse and keyboard, which greatly affects the image experience. 
The article analyzed the sensing methods of gesture recognition in detail and pointed out the development 
direction. Li et al.18 proposed a novel millimeter-wave radar point cloud gesture recognition methodology, this 
study considers the novel point cloud analysis framework for the enhancement of the recognition accuracy. Yu et 
al.19 proposed an algorithm combining 2D convolutional neural network and feature fusion for dynamic gesture 
recognition. The model uses original keyframes and optical flow keyframes to represent spatial and temporal 
features respectively. At the same time, the study uses fractional order method to extract optical flow map to 
reduce computational complexity.
Bhushan et al.20 conducted an experimental analysis on the application of various machine learning 
algorithms in gesture recognition. The study compared the latest algorithms such as Naive Bayes, K-nearest 
neighbor (KNN), random forest, XGBoost, and support vector machine (SVC). The results showed that CNN 
performed best in gesture recognition tasks. Cai et al.21 studied dynamic gesture recognition based on A-mode 
ultrasonic signals. The algorithm used the dynamic time warping (DTW) algorithm to match time series. At 
the same time, the model was further improved by extracting features through Gaussian filtering, principal 
component analysis (PCA) and other techniques. Wang et al.22 studied gesture recognition based on MEMS 
inertial sensors. The study used support vector machine (SVM), back propagation neural network (BP), decision 
tree (DT) and random forest (RF) for static gesture recognition. At the same time, hidden Markov model 
(HMM) and Attention-BiLSTM were used for dynamic gesture recognition. Xu et al.23 proposed a robust gesture

a multi-stream residual network (MResLSTM) for spatiotemporal feature extraction. At the same time, the

Experimental results show that the recognition effect of combining sEMG signals and acceleration signals is 
better than that of using sEMG signals alone. Zheng et al.30 studied an in-vehicle gesture recognition system 
based on frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar and Transformer network. The system first 
obtains the spatiotemporal features of gestures through radar signal processing and then classifies them through

Review of transformer models
The Transformer architecture has shown potential in areas such as the visual recognition, image de-raining, 
remote sensing image change detection, and point cloud video modeling. Li et al.31 studied the application of 
Transformer architecture in computer vision tasks. The study proposed a Contextual Transformer (CoT) module. 
This module encodes the context of the input key by introducing a 3 × 3 convolution, so that the attention matrix 
can utilize rich neighborhood information. Experimental results show that CoTNet performs well in tasks 
such as image recognition, object detection, instance segmentation, and semantic segmentation. Chen et al.32 
studied the application of Transformer in image deraining tasks. At the same time, the study proposed a sparse 
Transformer (DRSformer) model. The model uses an adaptive top-k selection operator to retain only the most 
valuable self-attention scores to optimize feature aggregation. At the same time, the model introduces a mixed-
scale feed-forward network to enhance the learning ability of multi-scale information. Zhang et al.33 proposed 
a pure Transformer network SwinSUNet for the problem of change detection in remote sensing images. The 
model adopts a Siamese U-shaped structure. The encoder extracts multi-scale features with a hierarchical Swin 
Transformer, and the fusion module merges the dual-temporal features for the final output.
Fan et al.34 studied the spatiotemporal modeling problem of point cloud videos. At the same time, the study 
proposed P4Transformer. This network combines point cloud 4D convolution and Transformer to avoid the 
limitations of traditional point tracking methods. Li et al.35 proposed TransUNetCD for the change detection 
problem of optical remote sensing images. This is a hybrid architecture that combines the advantages of 
Transformer and UNet. This method extracts local features through CNN and then uses Transformer to capture 
global context information. In the attention module, multi-scale features are fused through jump connections 
to improve detection accuracy. In addition, the model introduces a difference enhancement module, which can 
effectively suppress redundant information. Mishra et al.36 studied the problem of image anomaly detection 
and localization. The model combines the reconstruction method with the patch embedding technology of 
Transformer to preserve spatial information. At the same time, the abnormal area is located through the Gaussian 
mixture density network. Huo et al.37 studied the problem of traffic flow prediction. This study proposed a 
model that combines a hierarchical spatiotemporal graph convolutional network with Transformer. Although 
the traditional GCN method can handle the irregular topology of traffic networks, it is difficult to capture both 
short-term and long-term temporal relationships at the same time. To this end, this study used Transformer to 
enhance spatiotemporal feature modeling capabilities of GCN to improve prediction performance.
Plizzari et al.38 proposed a new spatiotemporal Transformer network (ST-TR) in their study. The model was 
used for skeleton-based action recognition. Skeleton data has high accuracy requirements due to its robustness 
to lighting changes, body proportions, dynamic perspectives and complex backgrounds. The study introduced 
a Transformer-based self-attention mechanism, in which the spatial self-attention module (SSA) was used to 
model the intra-frame interactions between different body parts. Che et al.39 studied the Transformer-based 
electrocardiogram (ECG) signal processing and arrhythmia classification problems. The study proposed an 
end-to-end deep learning framework that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Transformer 
networks. In addition, the study introduced a new chain-constrained loss function to enhance the classification 
ability of the embedding vector. Lian et al.40 proposed a Transformer-based dialogue emotion recognition

Th data acquisition and Pre-processing module
Depth sensor and hand image acquisition
The emergence of 3D sensors has made the human-computer interaction system based on gestures further 
successful. Microsoft’s Kinect device41 is one of the representatives. The Kinect device consists of an RGB 
camera, a depth sensor, and an infrared transmitter, which can capture the color and depth information of the 
scene in real time. The depth sensor can obtain 30 frames of images per second. The depth image is a graphical 
representation of the depth information of the scene. The grayscale value of each pixel represents the distance of 
the object from the camera. The smaller the value, the closer the scene is to the camera, and vice versa. The device 
used in this article is Kinect2.0, which is mainly composed of three sensors, namely infrared transmitter, color 
CMOS image sensor and infrared CMOS sensor. In addition, there are components such as the audio collector. 
The internal structure is shown in Fig. 2.
The data obtained by Kinect is 3D point cloud data. Point cloud is a massive point set that expresses the 
spatial distribution and surface characteristics of the target in the same spatial reference system. After obtaining 
the spatial coordinates of each sampling point on the surface of the object, a point set is obtained. Generally 
speaking, point clouds can be divided into sparse point clouds and dense point clouds according to the distance 
between points. Sparse point clouds are usually obtained by 3D coordinate measuring machines, and these point 
clouds are distant and sparse. Dense point clouds are obtained by 3D laser scanners or other scanners, and the 
obtained point cloud data is relatively compact.

The gesture detection and segmentation module with feature prior
Preliminary detection and segmentation of hand regions based on EfficientNet
In recent years, CNNs have achieved remarkable results in the field of hand segmentation, but CNN mainly 
focuses on local information, so we turn our attention to the Transformer, which has been successful in the 
field of natural language processing. An effective framework for extracting hand information is the Efficient 
Transformer model. Shallow features are linearly embedded and positionally encoded to obtain labeled image 
blocks. They are then transferred to the improved Transformer module to extract local and global features and 
suppress features with less information to enhance feature expression. The extracted deep feature map is used to 
extract multi-scale features through the spcASPP module. In the decoder stage, the shallow features obtained by 
CNN and the deep features obtained by the Transformer encoder are fused through jump connections. Finally, 
by splicing and fusing shallow features and deep features, we can capture the detailed information of the image 
and integrate high-level semantic information. In the Fig. 3, this typical structure is shown.

Integration of local pattern image feature prior
Local pattern prior can better assist the detection and segmentation of hand areas. Among the many local 
patterns, texture analysis is the most accurate prior knowledge. In this model, the ring-type hand image local 
binary pattern (RTHLBP) prior is considered. The basic idea of the algorithm is to compare the points with an 
interval of 1 in the clockwise direction with the pixel X1 to the upper left of the center pixel as the starting point 
within the 3 × 3 neighborhood.

More accurate discrimination: By comparing adjacent pixels pairwise along the ring, RTHLBP is able to

Stronger noise immunity: Pairwise comparison reduces sensitivity to subtle local changes and noise. These

Rotation tolerance: RI-LBP explicitly handles rotation, while RTHLBP uses circular comparison. This

The AR gesture mapping and acceleration module
Model acceleration for real-time schemes
Although the existing designed algorithms can stably recognize the gestures, augmented reality scenarios have 
high real-time requirements, so the real-time optimization is crucial. In this section, we will design a parallel 
computing paradigm for convolution kernels between DSP cores, also known as parallel computing in the 
input dimension. Vector accelerators are high-performance processors with bandwidth and computing power 
far exceeding embedded devices used for edge computing. Considering that the vectorization of convolution 
kernels greatly limits the versatility of the method, that is, the number of convolution kernels in the convolutional 
neural network must be an integer multiple of the number of VPEs, we store image data in AM, which means 
that the image data needs to be vectorized. The image vectorization method is shown in Fig. 10. For any three-
dimensional image, we can use the three-dimensional data block in the figure to represent it. The pixels in the 
image can be controlled by the three coordinates of length, width, and number of channels. We put the data 
with the same coordinates in different pictures in the same block. These images are aligned according to the 
width, length and dimension information. Then, the processor can read the image data row by row, reading 1024 
bits of data each time, which contains 64 16-bit data, that is, the number of pictures in the same batch in the 
calculation task is 64. During calculation, we transfer the data of these 64 pictures to the vector storage space, 
and then transfer the convolution kernel data to the scalar storage space. The convolution kernel data needs to 
be converted into a 64-dimensional vector according to the copy-expand-broadcast process. At this point, the 
preparation of convolution kernel data and the image data is completed.
For the Transformer model proposed in this study, the 3*3 convolution optimization is mainly considered. 
The variables of the convolution calculation mainly include image width, image length, number of image 
channels, length, width and number of channels of convolution kernel. In standard convolution, the number 
of channels of convolution kernel is equal to that of image. It can be seen that when the image size is fixed, the 
amount of calculation of convolution layer is directly related to the size of convolution kernel, and the use of 
small convolution kernel can effectively reduce the calculation time of the program. Therefore, this study designs 
a new double buffer mechanism framework in the convolution layer as shown in Table 2.
The on-chip vector storage space Transformer is divided into four areas A, B, C, and D. The data of the first 
dimension in the image is loaded into area A, and the data of the first dimension in the convolution kernel is 
used for calculation, and the result is stored in area B. Then the data of the second dimension in the image is 
loaded into area C, and its calculation result is stored in area D. This operation can minimize the amount of 
calculation and improve efficiency.

AR gesture mapping and interaction implementations
In order to facilitate the study of AR gestures, this paper uses the Vision Pro split AR head display launched by 
Apple, which is mainly composed of a mobile processing unit and a display, and the two parts are connected by 
a type-c data cable. The overall process of the framework includes three stages:
Stage 1  (1) Use the detection module in the framework to quickly determine whether the depth data contains a 
hand. (2) If there is no hand, continue to collect and determine. If there is a hand, the coordinate module in the 
framework further infers the 2D pixel coordinates of the index finger tip and the index finger root. (3) Obtain 
the 3D coordinates of the two joints of the index finger through the camera’s internal and external parameter 
conversion, and then draw a ray in the AR device that matches the user’s pointing.
Stage 2  In the second stage, when the ray collides with the AR virtual object, the virtual object is selected based 
on whether the collision lasts for 1 s, that is, whether the user is allowed to manipulate it. If the virtual object is 
selected, the index finger ray network stops judging the hand and predicting coordinates, stops ray drawing and 
collision detection, and enters the third stage of 2s time period action interaction.
Stage 3: When the index finger ray selects a virtual object, the user can make specific command actions to 
control the changes of the AR virtual object, such as: zoom in, zoom out, move left, move right, etc. When the 
command is “no operation”, the selection state of the virtual object will be released, and the index finger ray will 
continue to judge the hand and predict the coordinates.

Conclusion and future scopes
This study proposes a new algorithm based on local pattern perception of 3D video Swin Transformer combined 
with masked self-encoding. The algorithm can improve the real-time performance and gesture recognition 
accuracy of augmented reality gesture interaction to a certain extent. The proposed algorithm first uses the local 
attention mechanism of Swin Transformer to initially build the model. This operation effectively reduces the 
computational complexity while maintaining the global feature expression ability. At the same time, the masked 
self-encoding technology is combined in the recognition and classification stage, so that the model can learn 
time series patterns more efficiently. This operation can improve the recognition ability of the complex gestures. 
Experimental results show that compared with traditional gesture recognition algorithms, the algorithm 
proposed in this study has achieved good results in adaptive feature extraction, classification accuracy, time series 
modeling and computing resource optimization. At the hardware acceleration level, through reasonable multi-
core task scheduling and data parallel strategies, it is possible to reduce the computing time while maintaining 
high computing efficiency. As the number of DSP cores increases, the computing time is significantly reduced. 
However, the computing efficiency is slightly lower than that of single-core programs. This is mainly because 
multi-core computing requires additional parameter configuration and the critical path becomes longer with 
the increase in the number of cores. However, thanks to the local pattern perception ability and autoencoder 
optimization of Swin Transformer, the proposed algorithm can still maintain a high recognition accuracy 
under different degrees of parallelism. At the same time, it meets common requirements in terms of real-time 
performance. However, the current work still has 2 limitations:
	1.	 Although the proposed algorithm performs well in local pattern perception and temporal modeling, there is 
still room for improvement in its recognition accuracy for extremely complex or extremely diverse gestures.
2.The algorithm in this paper is mainly targeted at specific 3D video gesture data, and its generalization to other 
types of motion recognition or applications in different environments requires further verification.
Future research can be oriented toward the following optimization directions to further enhance the 
performance, robustness, and scalability of the proposed Swin Transformer-based gesture recognition 
framework:
